title: El Salvador Tax Incentives: Who Qualifies for Up to 10 Years of Relief?

lines: A tax incentive can improve your return.
But can it turn a weak location into a good investment?
Here's which incentive applies, who receives the benefit, and what remains after location and execution costs.
In El Salvador, qualifying new investments in San Salvador's defined Historic Center may receive up to ten years of income-tax relief.
That's a specific regime for a specific area, separate from nationwide programs.
Not every business qualifies, so verify current rules before underwriting.
Start with three checks.
First, exact location: inside the defined perimeter. One block outside can change the answer.
Second, a qualifying investment: an eligible activity, like food, lodging, or restoration, above the minimum.
Third, approval: the Historic Center's Planning Authority must qualify the project. No approval, no benefit.
Then ask: which entity receives the benefit?
Owner, operator, and developer are often different companies.
A landlord's qualification doesn't automatically lower a tenant's taxes.
Here's a simplified, hypothetical annual after-tax comparison.
Thirty thousand dollars of assumed tax savings, minus twenty-four thousand in additional after-tax occupancy costs, leaves six thousand a year.
It excludes other cost, timing, and risk differences. It's not a Salvadoran tax calculation, or a promised return.
Execution still matters: demand, permits, utilities, and opening delays can erase a thin advantage.
So underwrite the base case without incentives, then show the qualified benefit separately.
